title: A pathway‑centric classification strategy for robust and platform‑independent molecular subtyping of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma
text: Head Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma (HNSC) molecularly heterogeneous disease, classification distinct subtypes — Atypical, Basal, Classical, Mesenchymal — important implications prognosis therapeutic strategy. HNSCclassifier package provides ready--use tool assigning HNSC samples TCGA-established molecular subtypes. classifier employs pathway-level normalization strategy first converts gene expression profiles pathway enrichment scores via single-sample Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (ssGSEA), applies pre-trained random forest model final subtype prediction. design minimises cross-platform technical variation, making classifier applicable RNA-seq microarray data.

title: A pathway‑centric classification strategy for robust and platform‑independent molecular subtyping of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma
text: Command-line interface: classifyHNSC() batch prediction numeric gene expression matrix — ideal processing large cohorts integrating downstream pipelines. Interactive Shiny app: classifyHNSC_interface() users prefer graphical, point--click experience. Multi-platform identifier support: accepts gene symbols, Ensembl IDs, Entrez IDs, RefSeq accession numbers. Automatic conversion performed via org.Hs.eg.db. Flexible output: return predicted subtype class labels ("class") probability matrix ("prob") showing posterior probabilities four subtypes. Cross-platform robustness: designed work RNA-seq (TPM, FPKM, normalised counts) microarray expression data log2 transformation. Automatic preprocessing: input validation, log2 transformation detection application, gene-level noise reduction (zero-variance gene filtering) handled internally. Curated pathway gene sets: built carefully selected collection pathway gene sets (required.sets) ssGSEA, bridging input dataset model’s training feature space. Pre-trained random forest model: ships fully trained randomForest object (finalModel) — need users train tune model. Classification summary: summarize_subtype() quickly tabulates subtype distribution (counts, percentages, proportions) classification results. Gene ID conversion: convert_id() maps expression row names combination SYMBOL, ENSEMBL, ENTREZID, REFSEQ, configurable aggregation many--one mappings. Subtype-specific differential expression: extract_top_genes() runs one-vs-rest differential tests reveal marker genes molecular subtype. Confusion-matrix visualisation: plot_confusion_matrix() summarises classifier performance reference labels. HTML report generation: report_classification() compiles results figures single self-contained HTML report.

text: Gene expression data different bioinformatics pipelines often use different gene identifier systems. classifyHNSC() function supports four common identifier types via idType parameter: "SYMBOL" (default) — official HGNC gene symbols, e.g. TP53 "ENSEMBL" — Ensembl gene IDs, e.g. ENSG00000141510 "ENTREZID" — NCBI Entrez Gene IDs, e.g. 7157 "REFSEQ" — RefSeq accession numbers, e.g. NM_000546 idType "SYMBOL", function automatically maps input identifiers official gene symbols using org.Hs.eg.db annotation package. common scenario multiple input IDs map symbol handled retaining maximum expression value across duplicates, thereby preserving biologically informative signal. conversion, rest pipeline (log2 check, ssGSEA, random forest prediction) proceeds identically symbol-based input. built-dataset TCGA_LUSC_ENSEMBL provides ready--use example Ensembl identifiers.

text: find genes characterise given molecular subtype, extract_top_genes() performs one-vs-rest differential expression analysis: subtype, every gene compared samples subtype remaining samples. default test Wilcoxon rank-sum test, makes distributional assumptions; Welch t-test can selected instead method = "t.test". title: A pathway‑centric classification strategy for robust and platform‑independent molecular subtyping of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma
text: following code reads expression TSV, strips Ensembl version suffixes, converts Ensembl IDs gene symbols, retains primary tumour samples , filters zero-variance genes, runs classifyHNSC(). also fetches TCGA reference annotation downstream comparison.
code: library(data.table) library(org.Hs.eg.db) library(dplyr) library(tibble) library(stringr) library(TCGAbiolinks) library(HNSCclassifier)  # ---- 1. Read expression data ---- lusc.expr <- data.table::fread(   "TCGA-LUSC.star_tpm.tsv",   data.table = FALSE )  # Strip Ensembl version suffix (e.g. ENSG00000141510.11 → ENSG00000141510) lusc.expr$Ensembl_ID <- sapply(   lusc.expr$Ensembl_ID,   function(x) unlist(strsplit(x, "\\."))[1] )  # Convert Ensembl ID → gene symbol lusc.expr$symbol <- AnnotationDbi::mapIds(   org.Hs.eg.db,   keys      = lusc.expr$Ensembl_ID,   keytype   = "ENSEMBL",   column    = "SYMBOL" )  lusc.expr$Ensembl_ID <- NULL lusc.expr <- lusc.expr %>%   dplyr::filter(!is.na(symbol)) %>%   dplyr::group_by(symbol) %>%   dplyr::summarise_all(max) %>%   dplyr::ungroup() %>%   as.data.frame() %>%   tibble::column_to_rownames("symbol")  # Keep primary tumour samples only (barcodes ending with "-01A") lusc.expr <- lusc.expr[, grepl("01A$", colnames(lusc.expr))]  # ---- 2. TCGA subtype annotation ---- lusc.subtype <- TCGAbiolinks::TCGAquery_subtype(tumor = "LUSC") lusc.subtype$sample <- paste0(lusc.subtype$patient, "-01A") lusc.subtype <- lusc.subtype[   lusc.subtype$sample %in% colnames(lusc.expr), ] lusc.expr <- lusc.expr[, lusc.subtype$sample]  # Harmonise subtype labels to title case lusc.subtype$Expression.Subtype <- stringr::str_to_title(   lusc.subtype$Expression.Subtype )  # Remove zero-variance genes lusc.expr <- lusc.expr[apply(lusc.expr, 1, mad) > 0, ]  # ---- 3. Run HNSCclassifier ---- lusc_pred <- classifyHNSC(lusc.expr, outputType = "class") table(lusc_pred)

text: Command-line interface: classifyHNSC() batch prediction numeric gene expression matrix — ideal processing large cohorts integrating downstream pipelines. Interactive Shiny app: classifyHNSC_interface() users prefer graphical, point--click experience. Multi-platform identifier support: accepts gene symbols, Ensembl IDs, Entrez IDs, RefSeq accession numbers. Automatic conversion performed via org.Hs.eg.db. Flexible output: return predicted subtype class labels ("class") probability matrix ("prob") showing posterior probabilities four subtypes. Cross-platform robustness: designed work RNA-seq (TPM, FPKM, normalised counts) microarray expression data log2 transformation. Automatic preprocessing: input validation, log2 transformation detection application, gene-level noise reduction (zero-variance gene filtering) handled internally. Curated pathway gene sets: built carefully selected collection pathway gene sets (required.sets) ssGSEA, bridging input dataset model’s training feature space. Pre-trained random forest model: ships fully trained randomForest object (finalModel) — need users train tune model. Classification summary: summarize_subtype() generates concise summary table (counts, percentages, proportions) classification results, plus optional bar chart — quick overview subtype distribution cohort. Gene ID conversion: convert_id() maps expression matrix row names combination SYMBOL, ENSEMBL, ENTREZID, REFSEQ. Supports max/mean/median aggregation many--one mappings, automatic ENSEMBL version suffix stripping, optional retention unmapped genes. Subtype-specific differential expression: extract_top_genes() performs one-vs-rest differential expression analysis molecular subtype (Wilcoxon rank-sum test Welch’s t-test), returning genes pass user-defined log2 fold-change adjusted p-value thresholds — ideal biomarker discovery. One-click report generation: report_classification() compiles classification results, visualizations, optional differential expression analysis self-contained HTML report — suitable supplementary material publications clinical documentation.

title: Classify Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma Samples into TCGA Subtypes — classifyHNSC
text: function proceeds five main steps: Input validation: Checks missing values (NA), non-numeric columns, negative expression values, missing row/column names, correct sample number. Gene ID conversion (idType "SYMBOL"): Converts row identifiers gene symbols using org.Hs.eg.db. multiple identifiers map gene symbol, maximum expression value retained sample. Log2 transformation: data already log2 scale (determined internal heuristic), transformed log2(x + 1). Pathway-level representation: Single-sample gene set enrichment analysis (ssGSEA) performed using curated set pathway gene sets stored internally required.sets. step harmonizes input data training cohort biological pathway level. Random forest classification: pathway scores centered, scaled, fed pre-trained random forest model (finalModel) generate final subtype prediction. required.sets finalModel internal package data loaded automatically. function requires GSVA package.
